description:
The museum collections in Angers connect fine art and the history of the city, with holdings developed at the Logis Barrault from the end of the eighteenth century.

European painting, medieval and Renaissance decorative objects, and sculpture form important areas. The associated Galerie David-d’Angers provides a distinct focus on the sculptor’s work.

description:
The Musée des Beaux-Arts Jules-Chéret in Nice preserves collections shaped by state deposits and private gifts. Its scope ranges from early European painting to modern art.

French eighteenth-century painting, including the Van Loo family, is a notable strength. Later landscapes and portraits connect the collection with nineteenth- and twentieth-century artistic life.
